newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end cautious pit trade higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end cautious pit trade higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly higher following a session of cautious trading heading into key U.S. economic data Friday and the Tokyo meeting of U.S. and Japanese government officials.
Afternoon order flows stayed sparse, with brokers noting scant participation from funds or other big participants who periodically had played in yen Wednesday.
"It was dead," said one floor broker of closing trade. "The end of the day was real quiet. The market's a little nervous over (the possibility of) a bad (jobs) number."

A Reuters poll of economists was revised Thursday to show an average estimate of up 196,000 non-farm jobs, with a 5.2-percent jobless rate, a 0.4-percent increase in hourly earnings and a drop to 34.8 hours in the average workweek.
U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin will meet Friday in Tokyo with Japanese prime minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
The Swiss francs gained some ground on unwinding of spreads against other units, notably marks and sterling, floor brokers said.
"It was mainly the cross unwinding," said a broker, adding that Swiss hit its high about when the mark touched its low.
Pounds gained ground, with some linking its move up also to comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George.
He said the pace of domestic U.K. demand required some tightening even though that would hurt British exporters.
Televised remarks Thursday morning by Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin had little effect.
She said the U.S. economy did not slow in the first quarter as expected and was performing quite strongly.
Marks stayed buoyant after Germany's February industrial output rose 1.9 percent after January's 1.5-percent decline and suggesting Germany's economy remains on the mend.

Brokers said mark garnered added support from EMU-delay talk after BoE's George was quoted in a Belgium newspaper Thursday as saying he doubts Germany and France are ready to join EMU, and he argued for a delay to the 1999 startup.

Yen recouped some losses overnight, lifted when an official of Kampo said Kampo is wary of buying yen bonds because of low Japanese rates and its expectation that the dollar is unlikely to drop below 120 yen near term.
The International Monetary Fund in a paper prepared for a weekend Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting said some of the yen's recent depreciation may be reversed.

June yen settled up $0.000048 at $0.008243, marks gained $0.0036 to $0.6027, Swiss francs rose $0.0055 to $0.7034, sterling gained $0.0024 to $1.6440, Canadian dollar lost $0.0025 to $0.7222, Aussie dollar fell $0.0069 to $0.7765, and Mexican peso dropped $0.000475 to $0.121300.
